Port Authority Overview
• Since 1921, the Port Authority has moved the
region forward by managing and maintaining
vital trade and transportation links in the
following key business areas:
• Aviation
• Tunnels, Bridges & Terminals
• PATH
• Port
• World Trade Center

Port Authority’s Net Zero Roadmap
• In 2021, Port Authority embraced
Biden Administration’s GHG
reduction target of Net Zero by
2050, first U.S. transportation
agency to do so
• 50% agency-wide direct
emissions reduction by 2030,
cutting 137,000 tons annual
GHG emissions
• The Net Zero Roadmap, released
in September 2023, identifies
areas where we can act and where
we can influence

Zero Emissions Focus: Maritime Shipping
• Global shipping accounts for a
small percentage of global
Port of NYNJ
emissions
• Ships transit times can span
anywhere from a few days to over
30 days between ports
• Refueling is incredibly important
function of a port and typically
occurs at the same time as a vessel
is unloaded/loaded
• Other vessels including, cruise,
harbor craft, and offshore wind
vessels need fuel sources.

Summary of Freight Energy
Large challenges are ahead:
• Increasing demands for electrical infrastructure and supply to support
electrification
• Investment in the production and delivery of next generation fuels or vital for
freight
• Creation of new, sustainable, and reliable supply chains around the world
• Competitive disadvantage without local production and distribution.
• Lack of Sustainable fuel support from advocacy community
Opportunity Areas
• Significant number companies have or are working towards GHG or EV related
goals
• Incentives via legislation, and coordination with utilities, and municipalities
• Forging partnerships and cooperation between private and public sectors.
• Piloting of emerging technological solutions
